drivingQuestion: Why did the mishna have to state that women are obligated in Grace after Meals, when it is not a time-bound mitzva?
outcomeNote: The clause is justified: without it the verse fixing meal times would have made Grace after Meals a time-bound mitzva.

segments.he: וּבְבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן. פְּשִׁיטָא! מַהוּ דְתֵימָא הוֹאִיל וּכְתִיב ״בְּתֵת ה׳ לָכֶם בָּעֶרֶב בָּשָׂר לֶאֱכֹל וְלֶחֶם בַּבֹּקֶר לִשְׂבֹּעַ״, כְּמִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא דָּמֵי — קָמַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: We also learned in the mishna that women are obligated to recite the «Grace after Meals.» The Gemara asks: That too is «obvious.» The Gemara replies: «Lest you say: Since it is written: “When the Lord shall give you meat to eat in the evening and bread in the morning to the full”» (Exodus 16:8), one might conclude that the Torah established fixed times for the meals and, consequently, for the mitzva of Grace after Meals and, therefore, it «is considered a time-bound, positive mitzva,» exempting women from its recitation. Therefore, the mishna «teaches us» that women are obligated.
